topic_ko: 영국 통치로 자리 잡아 독립 후에도 공용어로 남은 남아시아 영어와, 힌디어와 섞이며 뜻이 변한 인도 영어(힝글리시)

passage: The varieties of English found in countries such as India, Pakistan, and Sri Lanka are called South Asian English.
The language first came to the Indian subcontinent in the early 17th century, and long years of British rule made its place even stronger.
Even today, some countries in the region use English as an official language.
India, for example, did not give up English after gaining independence, because it has hundreds of native languages besides Hindi.
With roughly 125 million speakers, Indian English is the best-known South Asian variety, and it is sometimes called "Hinglish," a blend of Hindi and English.
Speakers often add English words to Hindi, but the meanings of those words can shift as time passes.
In Indian English, would-be refers to the person someone is going to marry, and airdash means to travel somewhere quickly by plane.
choices: the decline of Hindi in modern India
why English became the only language of India
the history and features of English in South Asia
how air travel changed life in India
theme.explanation_ko: 영어가 남아시아에 들어와 자리 잡은 역사와, 힝글리시처럼 뜻이 변한 인도 영어의 특징을 다루므로 ③가 주제이다.
theme.distractor_ko: ① 힌디어가 쇠퇴한다는 말은 없다. ② 영어는 여러 언어 중 하나인 공용어일 뿐 유일한 언어가 아니다. ④ would-be 는 단어 뜻의 예일 뿐 결혼 풍습을 다루지 않는다. ⑤ airdash 는 단어 뜻의 예일 뿐이다.
